prompt: Stage 4-2, level 8, 40 HP. You just rolled 40 gold looking for a second copy of your 4-cost AD carry and found none, but you hit three copies of a 4-cost AP caster you were not looking for, now 2-star on the bench, and a 2-star 4-cost tank. You have 18 gold left. Your items are two completed AD items on the 1-star carry and one AP item unequipped. What now?

options.label: Put the 2-star caster in with the AP item, keep the 1-star carry as a second body, stop rolling and rebuild econ
Roll the last 18 gold: you are already committed and one copy fixes the board
Sell the caster for 8 gold and keep rolling for the carry with 26

explanation:
The rolldown answered a question you did not ask: the pool has AP casters and not AD carries. Three copies in 40 gold of rolling is the signal that other players are holding your carry, and 18 more gold at level 8 buys you nine shops, which is a coin flip for one copy that still leaves the carry 1-star if you miss. The 2-star caster with an AP item on it is a stabilised board right now, at 40 HP, against a lobby that is about to hit its own rolldowns.

The AD items are the cost of the pivot, and it is a smaller cost than it looks: they stay on the 1-star carry, which is still a reasonable second damage source at level 8, and you re-slot them when the board settles. Rolling to zero is the classic 4-2 death: no gold, no econ, one loss from 20 HP. Selling the caster to fund more rolling is worse, because it throws away the only hit you got.
principle: A rolldown that misses your target but hits something else is a pivot the pool chose for you. Take it.
commonMistake: Sunk cost: forty gold went into finding the carry, so the last eighteen must go there too.
